newsitem.title: THAILAND: Two Thai firms deny rumours of financial problems.
newsitem.headline: Two Thai firms deny rumours of financial problems.

text.p: SITCA Investment and Securities Plc and First City Investment Plc on Friday moved to calm market jitters about their financial positions and denied rumours they were facing client loan defaults.

They said in filings to the Stock Exchange of Thailand that their financial positions were stable and they had not been hurt by sales linked to the current bearishness in the Thai bourse, where the stock index opened at a near three-year-low.
The Thai bourse tumbled on Thursday after rumours that some Thai securities and finance companies may be affected by client loan defaults.

The stock market opened sharply lower on Friday, with the index starting at a near three-year-low of 1018.68 on weak sentiment as a result of the rumours and forced selling of stocks held by investors unable to meet margin loan call by brokers.
SITCA and First City were among some finance and brokerage firms hit by rumours they faced troubles from growing margin loan defaults by clients.
The rumours, denied by the stock exchange and the Bank of Thailand, triggered a heavy stock sell-off on Thursday.
SITCA, a licensed broker, said it had only 40 small clients who were forced by market regulations to sell shares to pay off loans owed to the company.
It said each of the indebted clients was required to sell shares worth no more than 100,000 baht (US$4,000) to cut losses.

SITCA also said it would not be hurt by any baht devaluation in the future as it had tapped an unspecified amount of a three-year foreign loan that had been fully covered against future foreign exchange losses.
First City said the bearish Thai bourse has not affected its finance business, which does not include securities broking, nor has it extended any margin loans to stock investors.
It said the company, backed by industrial investment bank Industrial Finance Corp of Thailand (IFCT.BK, saw its first half year profit rise to 139.9 million baht from 93.9 million a year ago.
